descriptor.scene: DAVID KOBROSKY stands at a rooftop garden rail at dusk, back three-quarter to the viewer's LEFT edge with his face in warm profile-adjacent three-quarter view looking out, one hand open toward the view as if introducing it. Below and beyond spreads a warm neighborhood: a dozen pools of gathering light: a backyard dinner, a lit church hall, a rooftop movie, a garage workshop, porches with neighbors, each a small circle of tiny distant figures. Between the circles run strings of festival lights like the yarn on his old corkboard, visually joining circle to circle. First stars. The city reads as a community of communities, catching everyone. Lower-right: deep calm dusk sky.
descriptor._caption: What works in a room works in the world. A society is a community of communities, and it has edges too, crowded with people slipping through cracks. Hyperagents can build the systems that notice them, welcome them in, and waste nobody. That is the world worth building toward.
descriptor.anonymous: Distant tiny neighborhood figures in the light circles, too small for faces; none distinct, none resembling David.
negatives: a second man resembling David near the camera
cold blue cityscape: every light is warm
